{{Short description|Criteria in Category theory of Mathematics}}
{{about|Freyd's adjoint functor theorem|Adjoint functor theorem for posets|Galois connection#Adjoint functor theorem for posets}}
In [[category theory]], a branch of mathematics, the '''formal criteria for adjoint functors''' are criteria for the existence of a left or right [[adjoint functors|adjoint]] of a given [[functor]].

One criterion is the following, which first appeared in [[Peter J. Freyd]]'s 1964 book ''Abelian Categories,<ref>{{harvnb|Freyd|2003|loc=Chapter 3. (pp.84–)}}</ref> an Introduction to the Theory of Functors'':
{{math_theorem|
name=Freyd's adjoint functor theorem<ref>{{harvnb|Mac Lane|2013|loc=Ch. V, § 6, Theorem 2.}}</ref>
|math_statement = Let <math>G: \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{A}</math> be a functor between categories such that <math>\mathcal{B}</math> is complete. Then the following are equivalent (for simplicity ignoring the set-theoretic issues):
# ''G'' has a left adjoint.
# <math>G</math> preserves all limits, and the following ''solution set condition'' is satisfied: for each object ''x'' in <math>\mathcal{A}</math>, there exist a set ''I'' and an ''I''-indexed family of morphisms <math>f_i : x \to G y_i</math> such that each morphism <math>x \to Gy</math> is of the form <math>G(y_i \to y) \circ f_i</math> for some morphism <math>y_i \to y</math>.
}}
Another criterion is:
{{math_theorem
| name = Kan criterion for the existence of a left adjoint
| math_statement = Let <math>G: \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{A}</math> be a functor between categories.  Then the following are equivalent.
# ''G'' has a left adjoint.
# ''G'' preserves [[limit (category theory)|limits]] and, for each object ''x'' in <math>\mathcal{A}</math>, the limit <math>\lim ({(x \downarrow G) \to \mathcal{B}})</math> exists in <math>\mathcal{B}</math>.<ref name=Kan>{{harvnb|Mac Lane|2013|loc=Ch. X, § 1, Theorem  2.}}</ref>
# The right [[Kan extension#Adjoints as Kan extensions|Kan extension]] <math>G_! 1_{\mathcal{B}}</math> of the identity functor <math>1_{\mathcal{B}}</math> along ''G'' exists and is preserved by ''G''.<ref>{{harvnb|Mac Lane|2013|loc=Ch. X, § 7, Theorem 2.}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Kelly|1982|loc=Theorem 4.81}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Medvedev|1975|page=675}}</ref>
Moreover, when this is the case then a left adjoint of ''G'' can be computed using the right [[Kan extension]].<ref name=Kan />
}}

== Proof ==
The idea is to construct a left adjoint directly as a limit.-->
